TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS

      DAY Monday training 60m "Intro Conditioning":
        warmup:
          walking 10 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          leg_press 2x12 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
          chest_press 2x12 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
          lat_pulldown 2x12 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
          seated_row 2x12 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          cycling 5 minutes

      DAY Wednesday training 40m "Mobility and Base Aerobic":

          walking 5 minutes

          goblet_squat 2x12 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
          dumbbell_row 2x12 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
          shoulder_press 2x12 rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          chair_stretch 5 minutes
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Friday training 45m "Light Conditioning + Core":
        warmup:
          cycling 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:

        main straight_sets:

NUTRITION PLAN
  NUTRITION_PLAN public
  OBJECTIVE "Cardiac health optimization: support lipid management, blood pressure stability, glycemic control, and sustainable energy for training; emphasize whole foods, fiber, lean proteins, healthy fats, and sodium moderation"

  GUIDING_PRINCIPLES
    - Focus on Mediterranean-style pattern: emphasis on vegetables, fruits, whole grains, legumes, lean proteins, olive oil, nuts; limit processed foods.
    - Daily energy: modest caloric balance to support training recovery; avoid excessive energy deficit.
    - Macronutrients: protein 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day; fats 25–35% of calories (rich in monounsaturated and polyunsaturated); carbohydrates to support training at moderate volumes; fiber 25–35 g/day.
    - Sodium: limit to roughly 1500–2300 mg/day depending on clinician guidance; monitor blood pressure.
    - Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg/day; adjust with activity.
    - Alcohol: if consumed, limit to moderate and avoid binge patterns; discuss with clinician.
    - CHD risk factors: minimize added sugars; maximize colorful fruits/vegetables; include plant sterols if appropriate.

  DAILY_STRUCTURE
    - Breakfast:
        protein_source: "egg_white_omelet" or "greek_yogurt" or "tofu_scramble"
        carb_source: "oats" or "whole_grain_bread"
        fats: "olive_oil" in cooking, "avocado" optional
        fiber: include fruit or veg
        example: "egg_white_omelet with spinach and tomato, oats with berries, olive_oil drizzle"
    - Lunch:
        protein_source: "grilled_chicken" or "salmon" or "legumes"
        carb_source: "quinoa" or "brown_rice" or "sweet_potato"
        vegetables: 2 servings
        fats: "olive_oil" dressing
        example: "grilled_chicken quinoa bowl with mixed vegetables and olive oil"
    - Dinner:
        protein_source: "turkey_meatballs" or "tofu_stir_fry" or "white_fish"
        carb_source: "barley" or "farro" or "cauliflower_rice" (low carb option)
        vegetables: color variety
        fats: "nuts" or "seeds" small portion
        example: "baked white fish with barley and roasted vegetables"
    - Snacks (2-3 daily, if needed):
        options: ["apple_with_nestle", "banana_with_natural_peanut_butter", "hummus_and_veg", "unsalted_nuts_small"] 
  SUPPLEMENTS (as advised by clinician)
    - Optional: fish_oil, fiber supplement, magnesium, potassium as per lab results and clinician guidance
  BEHAVIORAL_HEALTH
    - Mindful_eating: eat slowly, pause between bites
    - Meal_pref_timer: 1-2 meals/week allow occasional treat within budget
  MONITORING
    - Track weight weekly; note energy, sleep, and exertion
    - If symptoms or BP issues arise, adjust sodium and hydration, and consult clinician
  COORDINATION_WITH_MAINTENANCE
    - Align nutrition with training phases; adjust calories around longer aerobic days
  SAMPLE_DAY_PLAN
    DAY 1:
      BREAKFAST: "egg_white_omelet with spinach and tomato, oats with berries, olive oil"
      LUNCH: "grilled_chicken quinoa bowl with mixed vegetables and olive oil"
      DINNER: "baked_white_fish with barley and roasted vegetables"
      SNACKS: "apple_with_natural_peanut_butter", "hummus_and_veg"
  NOTES
    - All nutrition choices should be reviewed with client’s medical team to ensure compatibility with post-MI status and current medications.
    - Prioritize foods with low added sugars and high fiber; choose whole-food sources over ultra-processed options.
